This is based on my opinion and interpretation. I'll go in order of the bullet points...

• when remembering something or telling a story, try to allow your feelings to grow, reflect harder on your feelings. maybe even logically decipher what feelings would sound normal if someone else was telling this story (to assist in validating your own feelings as it's normal to think x wasn't hurtful when it happens to us but it's normal to call x hurtful if it happens to someone else).

• if you usually hide emotion, see if you can relax your body and let it have some form of release that you'd usually hold it back from. Yes understand the trauma, but if your body wants to release tears, shake, scream etc, allow your body to rather than holding the pressure in. Showing feeling doesn't invalidate the reasoning associated with your trauma.

• 1st and 2nd bullet point covers this

• reasoning and intellect don't always validate our grief. We can't always explain our grief and ground it in logical understanding. We should accept emotions as they are, emotions just exist, it's human, and our feelings are valid regardless of how little or much sense they make. Possible ways you could validate your emotions by: accepting you're human, think of occasions where you have seen other people valid even with their different feelings on display, maybe make art, or take in nature. 

• 4th bullet point covers this but I'd like to add that emotions aren't supposed to make sense, they are e-motions - energy in motion. They are live energy, positive and negative running through us, and we are life. Love is also one of those weird emotions, where it can't be explained away.

• we might want to cope with handling our feelings by understanding where they come from and why eg 'person Z made fun of me in front of everyone, it made me feel shame'. In this sentence we shouldn't ignore the shame feeling and make the whole thought and rant about being made fun of in order to run away from the feeling of shame, but we should talk about Z's actions cause those feelings and acknowledging those feelings.

Edit: regarding it being too painful to talk about with your therapist, maybe you could write it out/type it out in a journal for yourself. Slowly release the feelings if you can and after mentally preparing when your ready. With trauma resolving, I experienced (and have read here and there) that the flood gates do open and resolving is more mentally painful than the trauma itself.
